perCase.question: Why does cortex-ide forbid CSS classes and require inline styles?

full.answer: The rule exists because of an **iOS Safari reliability issue** — CSS class-based styling is not predictable in webview environments (Tauri, PWA) [D-spec-ingest:cortex-ide:docs-prompts-codex-sprint-1-orchestrator-loop:codebase-rules-mandatory]. The rule is marked **permanent** [FACT-37b7c497-66c0-4f88-9880-b600118f9ef7]. Note that desktop components (`command-center-shell.tsx`, `session-operator-panel.tsx`, `workflow-review-panel.tsx`) are exempt and *do* use CSS classes from `globals.css` for grid-based responsive layouts [D-spec-ingest:cortex-ide:docs-conventions:styling].

perCase.question: Why did the team choose FTS5 + structured SQL over a vector store for the Cortex Q&A retrieval layer?

full.answer: The decision was driven by the OSS-Cortex post-mortem, which showed **88/501 real embeddings and 413 silent fallbacks to zero-vectors under load** — the embedding pipeline degraded without any error signal [CMT-issue-915-4347800077]. The team's explicit conclusion was that BM25 has no silent-failure mode (it returns ranked tokens or nothing), while FTS5 BM25 is in-process, sub-200ms, and indexed-on-write via SQLite triggers with no async embedding worker to go wrong [CMT-issue-915-4347800077]. Vector retrieval was also judged as the wrong abstraction for the task — it returns opaque blobs, whereas the new system needs typed rows with citation handles so the LLM composer can detect contradictions across facts ("D-014 says X but O-481 did Y") rather than just blend embeddings [CMT-issue-915-4347800077]. This maps to the founder's "brain not memory" framing: memory = vector blobs (what OSS-Cortex shipped), brain = composition over operator-curated typed rows with a contradiction pass [CMT-issue-915-4347800077]. The decision was also reinforced by a direct rule that vector similarity must not be used for selection ranking — characterized as overkill, the wrong tool, and the wrong stack for this context [FACT-4cf9122e-babf-49b7-b827-93d42015b3cc].

perCase.question: What is the locked LLM routing strategy for Cortex Q&A — which model handles lookup vs reasoning?

full.answer: The Cortex Q&A routing is a locked two-tier system [CITATION:fact-e627904b-52e7-4bbf-b672-dd0bad3c67c6]: **Class A (Lookup)** is handled by **Gemini 2.5 Flash** (200–500ms total), and **Class B (Reasoning)** is handled by **Claude Sonnet** streaming (1–3s total). perCase.question: How do we ship a new release of the o8 desktop app — what command sequence does the daily-driver loop use?

full.answer:
The daily-driver loop uses this four-command sequence [D-spec-ingest:cortex-ide:claude:shipping-dev-prod-mode-the-daily-driver-loop:the-loop]:

```bash
nvm use                  # pins Node 22 LTS (hard requirement — release.mjs fails if node !== 22.x)
npm version patch        # bumps 0.1.X → 0.1.X+1; sync-version.mjs hook syncs package.json,
                         # tauri.conf.json, and Cargo.toml in one commit, then tags v0.1.X+1
git push --follow-tags   # pushes the version bump commit + the new tag to origin
npm run ship             # cargo tauri build with signing key + dev-mcp-plugin feature,
                         # then scripts/release.mjs creates the GH release and uploads all 4 assets
```

After `npm run ship` completes, the installed `/Applications/o8.app` picks up the new version via the `UpdateBanner` component (polls every 30 min or on launch), downloads the signed `.app.tar.gz`, verifies the minisign signature against the pubkey in `tauri.conf.json`, replaces the app, and relaunches [D-spec-ingest:cortex-ide:claude:shipping-dev-prod-mode-the-daily-driver-loop:the-loop].

The signing key lives at `~/.tauri/cortex-ide.key` — don't rotate it without re-signing every future release or the installed app will reject the update [D-spec-ingest:cortex-ide:claude:shipping-dev-prod-mode-the-daily-driver-loop:signing]. CI is bypassed because GitHub Actions macOS runners have billing issues; local `npm run ship` takes ~2–4 min vs ~6 min CI [D-spec-ingest:cortex-ide:claude:shipping-dev-prod-mode-the-daily-driver-loop:why-local-instead-of-ci].
